<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Sp1nd01" /></noinclude>and two yeeres, and begate ſonnes and daughters.

{{Verse|5|27}} And all the dayes of Methuſelah were nine hundred, ſixtie and nine yeeres, and he died.

{{Verse|5|28}} ¶ And Lamech liued an hundred eightie and two yeeres: and begate a ſonne.

{{Verse|5|29}} And he called his name ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=ǁ''Gr. Noe.''}} Noah, ſaying; This {{smaller|ſame}} ſhall comfort vs, concerning our woorke and toyle of our hands, becauſe of the ground, which the LORD hath curſed.

{{Verse|5|30}} And Lamech liued, after hee begate Noah, fiue hundred ninetie and fiue yeeres, and begate ſonnes and daughters.

{{Verse|5|31}} And all the dayes of Lamech were ſeuen hundred ſeuentie and ſeuen yeeres, and he died.

{{Verse|5|32}} And Noah was fiue hundred yeeres olde: and Noah begate Sem, Ham, and Iapheth.

==={{Chapter|6|CHAP. VI.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#6:1|1]] The wickedneſſe of the world, which prouoked Gods wrath, and cauſed the Flood. [[#6:8|8]] Noah findeth grace. [[#6:13|13]] The order, forme, and end of the Arke.}}

{{Verse|6|1|notext=}} {{dropinitial|A|image=King James Bible (1611) page A2v (A).png|imgsize=100px}}Nd it came to paſſe, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and Daughters were borne vnto them:

{{Verse|6|2}}That the ſonnes of God ſaw the Daughters of men, that they {{smaller|were}} faire, and they took them wiues, of all which they choſe.

{{Verse|6|3}} And the LORD ſaid, My Spirit ſhall not alwayes ſtriue with man; for that hee alſo {{smaller|is}} fleſh: yet his dayes ſhallbe an hundred and twenty yeeres.

{{Verse|6|4}} There were Giants in the earth in thoſe daies: and alſo after that, when the ſonnes of God came in vnto the daughters of men, ⁊ they bare {{smaller|children}} to them; the ſame {{smaller|became}} mightie men, which {{smaller|were}} of old, men of renowme.

{{Verse|6|5}} ¶ And God ſaw, that the wickednes of man {{smaller|was}} great in the earth, and ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, the whole imagination. The Hebr. word ſignifieth not onely the imagination, but alſo the purpoſes and deſires.''}} {{smaller|that}} euery imagination of the thoughts of his *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chap. [[#8:21|8. 21.]]. mat.15.19}} heart {{smaller|was}} onely euill †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. euery day.''}} continually.

{{Verse|6|6}} And it repented the LORD that he had made man on the earth, and it grieued him at his heart.

{{Verse|6|7}} And the LORD ſaid, I will deſtroy man, whom I haue created, from the face of the earth: †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=''Hebr. from man vnto beast,''}} both man and beaſt, and the creeping thing, and the foules of the aire: for it repenteth me that I have made them.

{{Verse|6|8}} But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

{{Verse|6|9}} ¶ Theſe {{smaller|are}} the generations of Noah: *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Ecclus.44.17.2 pet.2.5}} Noah was a iuſt man, {{smaller|and}} ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, vp-right.''}} perfect in his generations, {{smaller|and}} Noah walked with God.

{{Verse|6|10}} And Noah begate three ſonnes: Sem, Ham, Iapheth.

{{Verse|6|11}} The earth alſo was corrupt before God; and the earth was filled with violence.

{{Verse|6|12}} And God looked vpon the earth, and behold, it was corrupt: for all fleſh had corrupted his way vpon the earth.

{{Verse|6|13}} And God ſaid vnto Noah, The end of all fleſh is come before mee: for the earth is filled with violence through them: and behold, I will deſtroy them ǁ{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=ǁ ''Or, from the earth.''}} with the earth.

{{Verse|6|14}} ¶ Make thee an Arke of Gopher-wood: †{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. nests''}} roomes ſhalt thou make in the arke, and ſhalt pitch it within and without with pitch.

{{Verse|6|15}} And this is {{smaller|faſhion}}, which thou ſhalt make it of: the length of the arke {{smaller|ſhalbe}} three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirtie cubits.

{{Verse|6|16}} A window ſhalt thou make to the arke, and in a cubite ſhalt thou finish it abooe; and the doore of the arke ſhalt thou ſet in the ſide thereof: With lower, ſecond, and third ſtories ſhalt thou make it.

{{Verse|6|17}} And behold, I, even I doe bring a flood of waters vpon the earth, to deſtroy all fleſh, wherein is the breath of life from vnder heauen, {{smaller|and}} every thing that is in the earth ſhall die.

{{Verse|6|18}} But with thee wil I eſtablish my Couenant: and thou ſhalt come into the Arke, thou, and thy ſonnes, and thy wife, and thy ſonnes wiues with thee.

{{Verse|6|19}} And of euery liuing thing of all fleſh, two of euery {{smaller|ſort}} ſhalt thou bring into the Arke, to keepe {{smaller|them}} alive with thee: they ſhall be male and female.

{{Verse|6|20}} Of fowles after their kinde, and of cattel after their kinde: of euery creeping thing of the earth after his kinde, two of euery {{smaller|sort}} ſhall come vnto thee, to keepe {{smaller|them}} alive.

{{Verse|6|21}} And take thou vnto thee of all food that is eaten, and thou ſhalt gather {{smaller|it}} to thee: and it ſhall be for food,<noinclude></noinclude>
